3.text:
In a Reversi move the disks which are turned over by a move $X$ are the
white disks which lie on a straight orthogonal or diagonal line through $X$
and which are bounded on the far side of the line by a black disk.  On the
board that is drawn the only non–trivial material is the little block which
lies in the south–east corner of the board.  In the co–ordinates which are
used in the drawing the block is

* $F_{16},G_{16},H_{16},I_{16}$ = $B$,
* $I_{17},I_{18},I_{19}=W$, $I_{20}=B$,
* $J_{13},J_{14}=B$, $J_{15}\dots J_{19}=W$, $J_{20}=B$,
* $K_{13}\dots K_{17}=W$, $L_{13}\dots L_{17}=W$,
* $M_{16}=B$, $M_{17},M_{18},M_{19}=W$,
* $N_{16}=B$, $N_{17},N_{18},N_{19}=W$,

and the rest of the board is empty.  Up to symmetry the only non–trivial
legal first player moves are the squares which sit on the open side of the
white block.  The longest white interval which is bounded on the far side
by a black man is the white interval which lies on the first diagonal of
the block.  For example on the diagonal

$$I_{16}=B\;,\;J_{17}=W\;,\;K_{18}=W\;,\;L_{19}=W\;,\;M_{20}\;$$

the three white men $J_{17},K_{18},L_{19}$ are sandwiched between the black
men $I_{16}$ and the black man which closes the block on the south–east
side, and the same configuration is repeated on the three parallel
diagonals which make up the staircase.  Adding the horizontal and the
vertical intervals which meet in the corner of the block one obtains the
usual Reversi “corner’’ move

\[
E_{16}\;{\rm or}\;H_{15}\;{\rm etc.}
\]

which turns over the whole of the white staircase.  In the normal
convention the move is quoted as the $13$ white men which can be turned over
in the one move, $5$ of them horizontally and $8$ of them on the two
diagonals which meet in the same square; in the strict orthogonal
counting which is usually quoted for the board as drawn the orthogonal
part of the move is the $5$–man horizontal turn over in the $J$–row,
$J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}$, between the black men $J_{14}$ and $J_{20}$, i.e. the
maximal orthogonal capture on the board is the $5$–man capture, and with
the two diagonals which meet in the same square the total number of white
men which can be captured in a single black move is the $12\!-\!13$ men
staircase which is usually quoted as $13$ white men.  This is the
maximal capture which the position allows; up to the conventional
$12/13$ counting it is the $5$–man horizontal $J_{15}$–$J_{19}$ capture,
the $13$–man $5+8$ capture being the maximal total capture of the
position.  The $5$–man horizontal capture is the one which is normally
quoted as the “largest’’ pure orthogonal capture, viz. the $5$ white disks
$J_{15},J_{16},J_{17},J_{18},J_{19}$ between the black men $J_{14}$ and
$J_{20}$.

*Remark.*  In the strict orthogonal convention the biggest pure
horizontal/vertical capture that can be made on the diagram is the
five–man capture $J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}$ between the black men $J_{14}$ and
$J_{20}$.  If the two diagonals which meet in the same corner square are
counted together the total number of white men which can be turned over
in a single black move is the $13$–man staircase, $12$ men in the most
common orthogonal–only counting.  This is the maximal Reversi capture
available to Black in the position shown.
